reconstructed_theorem: Let E and F be arbitrary complete real inner-product spaces, with their associated norms, of any dimension. Let f:F->R and g:E->F be everywhere Frechet differentiable maps, let alpha,sigma be real constants satisfying alpha>0 and sigma>=0, and let z be in F. Assume f is globally alpha-strongly convex: for all u,v in F and t in [0,1], f((1-t)u+tv)<=(1-t)f(u)+tf(v)-(alpha/2)t(1-t)||v-u||^2. Assume g is surjective onto all of F, and z is a global minimizer of f, meaning f(z)<=f(y) for every y in F. Finally assume the uniform derivative coercivity bound: for every x in E and v in F, sigma||v||^2 <= <v,Dg(x)(Dg(x)*v)>_F, where Dg(x):E->F is the actual continuous linear Frechet derivative and Dg(x)*:F->E is its Hilbert-space adjoint. Then there exists xstar in E such that g(xstar)=z, (f o g)(xstar)<=(f o g)(x) for every x in E, and for every x in E one has 2 alpha sigma [(f o g)(x)-(f o g)(xstar)] <= ||gradient(f o g)(x)||_E^2. The gradient is the Riesz representative of the derivative in E. The same chosen xstar satisfies all three conclusions, and the inequality is global and uses the same uniform alpha and sigma from the assumptions. The existence of a minimizer z of f is assumed rather than established; the theorem supplies a preimage minimizer for the composition. It does not assert uniqueness of that preimage minimizer, convexity or strong convexity of the composition, injectivity or linearity of g, continuity of either derivative, finite dimensionality, or any algorithmic convergence claim. In particular sigma may be zero, in which case the displayed gradient bound has zero on the left and gives no positive Polyak-Lojasiewicz constant.
